acceptance: The owner has decided to change the Presto-family 1_v7 shape (see context); if not, this item is dropped by the owner and nothing below applies

The Presto-family 1_v7 text builds one array of ROW values (alignment intrinsic) and, by the harness at a recorded clean commit, passes at SF1, SF2 and SF3 on Trino under stock limits (1.80 GB per node on a 6 GiB heap) with results equal to canonical Q1 within 1e-8; SF3 fails today

Peak user memory per run is recorded for each scale and compared with the 760-835 MiB per SF baseline in _project/audits/tpchavoc-q1-array-scale-2026-10-22.md; the ORDER BY keep-or-drop decision is made from those harness numbers; if the gain is not real the change is abandoned and the result recorded
Presto, Trino and Athena rendering assertions (tests/unit/tpchavoc/test_presto_compat.py and the sql_compat golden corpus entries for 1_v7) describe the new shape
The documentation added by PR 3547 (memory requirement of 1_v7 on Presto, Trino and Athena) is merged and its figures are updated to the new shape's measured numbers
context:
BLOCKED on an owner decision about whether to change the Presto-family 1_v7 shape at all. The owner asked (2026-10-26) whether this is worth fixing, whether it breaks comparability, and what SQL a naive Trino/Presto user would write. A read-only brief answered:
- Not a Presto translation bug. Memory linear in rows is inherent to the variant: it is the only array/lambda variant of 220 and builds four lists per Q1 group on every engine. DuckDB (the engine it is written for), local, DuckDB 1.5.5: canonical Q1 84 MiB at SF1 and 190 MiB at SF3; 1_v7 as written 902 and 2688 MiB (10.7x and 14.1x); four ordered lists 1419 and 3732 MiB (16.9x and 19.6x); one struct list 766 and 2296 MiB; ordered struct list 1179 and 3720 MiB; four lists plus unnest and GROUP BY 470 and 1345 MiB. Process-level footprint, indicative only. Trino 484 measured 760-835 MiB per SF, matching DuckDB's about 890 MiB per SF. PrestoDB 0.298.1 (Java) measured about 1.9 GiB per SF (HashAggregationOperator SINGLE;ORDER_BY;), 2.4x the Trino figure, and its default per-node limit (10% of heap, 614.4 MB at 6 GiB) fails 1_v7 at SF1; this was measured after the brief was written (see tpchavoc-native-engine-verification and the unpushed audit _project/audits/tpchavoc-prestodb-variants-2026-10-26.md on branch test/tpchavoc-prestodb-variant-verification). The constant-factor gain of a ROW array on PrestoDB was not measured.
- Changing to one ROW array (shape b) is a constant factor only. Probe on the old UNNEST text on Trino 476: 1.7-1.9x (not re-tested on the current REDUCE text). Estimated to move stock Trino from SF2 to about SF3-SF4 (inference); never SF10. Chunking by GROUP BY or UNION ALL slicing gave no reduction. Unnest-then-GROUP BY (c) and plain aggregation (d) stop exercising list lambdas and are rejected.
- Comparability: validation compares result rows only (validate_query1_results, equivalence.find_divergences), not SQL text. No published bundle has a 1_v7 row for Presto, Trino or Athena (only three DuckDB bundles); Databricks and BigQuery skip 1_v7; Spark, PostgreSQL, SQLite and DataFusion already use different shapes. TPC-Havoc results are not combined with TPC-H power/throughput scores; docs say judge optimizer robustness by timing spread and make no absolute cross-engine claims.
- Scope: 1 of 220 variants; CLI default SF is 0.01, docs call SF1 standard and SF10 stress; stock Trino fails from SF3; Presto C++ would fail from about SF0.035 because of the 100,000-element REDUCE cap (untested, see tpchavoc-native-engine-verification).
- Idiom: reduce over array_agg is the documented way to sum an array on Trino/Presto/Athena (Athena docs recommend it over UNNEST+SUM); shape (b) is more typical than the fork's NULL-guarded CASE folds and four sorts.
Brief recommendation (high confidence on diagnosis, medium on gain size): do not treat as a memory bug; document; optionally switch to shape (b) without ORDER BY as a cheap constant-factor change. Route if approved: a BenchBox-side Presto/Trino/Athena-only override in translate_list_aggregate_variant (benchbox/core/tpchavoc/dialect_compat.py) through the dialect_utils registry (the vendored-SQLGlot bypass test forbids direct use), or a fork change in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-sqlglot (compat.py order_list_aggregates/reduce_list_aggregates) plus a wheel bump via scripts/sync_sqlglot_runtime.py. Tests and goldens to update: tests/unit/tpchavoc/test_presto_compat.py (shape assertions) and tests/unit/sql_compat/golden_corpus/recorded/area_variants.json (presto, trino, athena). Re-measure on the current text with tpchavoc_trino_q1_scale_check.py at a clean commit before claiming any gain; if there is no gain, stop.

OWNER DECISION (2026-10-26): for SF3 and above the benchmark keeps running 1_v7 on Presto, Trino and Athena (no skip, no scale gate); the memory requirement is documented only. That documentation is PR 3547 (docs/benchmarks/tpc-havoc.md), open, with Trino and PrestoDB figures, and conflicting textually with PR 3545.

NEXT: the owner decides on the shape change. If no, drop this item (a human decision). If yes, claim it and follow the route above.
description: The 1_v7 text for Presto, Trino and Athena (the fork's order_list_aggregates + reduce_list_aggregates rewrites: four ordered ARRAY_AGG columns reduced with REDUCE/ZIP_WITH, develop #3326) exceeds Trino's default per-node memory limit from SF3. On Trino 484 with a 6 GiB heap it passes at SF1 (about 800 MiB) and SF2 (about 1.6 GiB, 87% of the 1843 MiB cap) and fails with EXCEEDED_LOCAL_MEMORY_LIMIT at SF3 and SF10, while canonical Q1 needs under 16 MiB. Memory is linear in rows, 760-835 MiB per scale factor, dominated by HashAggregationOperator ARRAY_AGG state. See the context of tpchavoc-q1-array-scale-check and _project/audits/tpchavoc-q1-array-scale-2026-10-22.md (merged in PR 3310). A probe on the earlier UNNEST text showed one ARRAY_AGG of ROW values cut peak memory about 1.7-1.9x, whereas chunking by GROUP BY or UNION ALL slicing gave no reduction; that factor is not yet re-tested on the current REDUCE text. This does not make memory bounded. Do not claim more. The rewrite lives in the fork, so the change is a fork/rule change plus a BenchBox pin.
